scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8058: Hi IT!! The upstairs design floor's 172.16.30.x
machines have STOPPED EXISTING for us downstairs -- from my PC5, 172.16.10.x,
every one of them times out, while my own floor is totally fine!! Something
around the big switch that joins the floors must be wrong, but I don't know
what. Could someone look at it and reconnect me to design -- deadlines!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. mswitch0 owns the L3 SVIs for VLAN 10/20/30
  (172.16.10.254 / 172.16.20.254 / 172.16.30.254) and routes between them; a
  VLAN 10 host reaches a VLAN 30 host with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / inter-VLAN
  fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- VLAN 10 cannot reach
VLAN 30 within Campus 1 -- is NOT reproducible: mswitch0's SVIs (172.16.10.254,
172.16.30.254) are up, and a VLAN 10 host (PC5) reaches a VLAN 30 host
(172.16.30.x) with 0% loss via mswitch0.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-VLAN routing on mswitch0 is
healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
VLAN10->VLAN30 path, finds it working, checks the SVIs on mswitch0, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a down/misconfigured SVI to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I could not reproduce the reported outage. Inter-VLAN reachability between the 172.16.10.0/24 (“downstairs”) and 172.16.30.0/24 (“design floor”) segments is currently healthy. From PC5 (172.16.10.5) I successfully pinged multiple design hosts (172.16.30.12/.13/.14) with 0% packet loss and low latency. Return packets show ttl=63, which is exactly what we expect for one routed hop between VLANs. PC5’s default gateway (172.16.10.254) is reachable and responsive from PC5, and design hosts have correct default routes via 172.16.30.254. Reverse pings (172.16.30.12 to 172.16.10.5) also succeed with 0% loss.

Affected component: none at this time; inter-VLAN routing and the aggregation switch path (mswitch0 -> switch1/switch3 and router gateway) are functioning.

Mechanism: traffic from 172.16.10.5 to 172.16.30.x is routed via the default gateway, traverses the inter-floor aggregation, and returns normally.

Localization: All tested endpoints on VLAN10 (PC5/6/7/8) reach VLAN30 (PC12/13/14) successfully; gateways .10.254 and .30.254 respond as expected. No device shows loss.

Root cause: Not reproducible now; the original symptom appears to have been transient or external to the campus network.

Corrective fix: No action required. Recommend the user re-test. If the issue recurs, capture timing, target IPs, and whether it affects all 30.x hosts. We can enable short-term monitoring on mswitch0/router16 interfaces to catch any intermittent flaps if needed.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes mswitch0's VLAN 10/30 SVIs are up and inter-VLAN routing works at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly notes that the gateways 172.16.10.254 and 172.16.30.254 are reachable and inter-VLAN routing between VLAN10 and VLAN30 is functioning at baseline.

The agent's tests (host configs and multiple bidirectional pings) directly support the conclusion that inter‑VLAN routing is working; assertions about gateway reachability and successful return paths follow logically from the observed ping results. The only minor gap is that explicit SVI status on mswitch0 wasn't shown, but the gateway and inter‑VLAN connectivity evidence sufficiently demonstrate no anomaly.
